feed.title: Western Digital, FormFactor, Penguin Solutions, Himax, and Power Integrations Shares Are Falling, What You Need To Know
feed.summary: Shares of several semiconductor companies, including Western Digital, FormFactor, Penguin Solutions, Himax, and Power Integrations, fell after benchmark 10-year U.S. Treasury yields rose above 5.1%, impacting high-multiple technology valuations. The market reacted to the bond yield increase, driven by a stronger-than-expected September composite purchasing managers' index, and concerns about supply competition and investor positioning in the semiconductor sector. Despite the dip, some companies like Western Digital have seen significant gains year-to-date.

feed.title: Cavco CEO unveils manufactured home without steel chassis at National Mall showcase
feed.summary: Cavco Industries has introduced a new manufactured home design that eliminates the traditional steel chassis, allowing homes to sit closer to the ground and appear more like site-built residences. This innovation, showcased at the National Mall, aims to enhance aesthetics and accessibility, addressing common criticisms of older manufactured homes. Despite these advancements, the article notes that zoning hurdles for these types of homes still persist.

feed.title: Oklo’s Isotope Test Reactor achieves criticality
feed.summary: Oklo's Groves Isotope Test Reactor has achieved criticality, becoming the fifth Department of Energy-authorized reactor to do so. This significant milestone was reached in Lockhart, Texas, in less than a year from a greenfield site, setting a new benchmark for advanced nuclear deployment. The project is part of Oklo Isotopes' broader strategy to build domestic isotope production facilities for various applications, including health care and national security.

feed.title: Texas Pacific Land extends executive contracts and announces 2027 annual meeting date

Dobbs—through the end of 2029, with automatic one-year extensions. feed.title: Eastman hosts community meeting on Choccolocco PCB remediation
feed.summary: Eastman Chemical Company will host a public meeting on Tuesday, September 29, at the Bynum Community Center to discuss the next phase of PCB remediation in and around Choccolocco Creek. The meeting will feature a presentation on understanding contaminant movement through sediment and surface water, and Eastman representatives will provide updates on upcoming activities and project milestones. Community members will have the opportunity to ask questions and learn more about the ongoing remediation efforts.

feed.title: ROSEN, A LEADING INVESTOR RIGHTS LAW FIRM, Encourages AppLovin Corporation Investors to Secure Counsel Before Important Deadline in Securities Class Action - APP
feed.summary: Rosen Law Firm has announced a class action lawsuit against AppLovin Corporation (NASDAQ: APP) on behalf of investors who purchased securities between February 12, 2026, and August 5, 2026. The lawsuit alleges that AppLovin made false or misleading statements regarding the development and benefits of its AI models for the AppLovin Ads platform. Investors are encouraged to secure counsel before the lead plaintiff deadline of November 16, 2026.

feed.title: A 17% premium to the 12-month average closing price: Utah Medical Products (UTMD) offers to buy shares.
feed.summary: Utah Medical Products, Inc. (UTMD) has announced a tender offer to purchase up to 650,000 shares of its common stock at $75.00 per share, representing a 17% premium over the last twelve months' average closing price. Despite a recent decline in sales and net profits, the company's board approved the offer to provide liquidity for shareholders, though it makes no recommendation on tendering shares. CEO Kevin Cornwell believes the shares are currently undervalued, suggesting a fair trading range of $90 per share based on industry valuation multiples.

feed.title: AI agents at Dreamforce 2026: from demos to outcomes
feed.summary: At Dreamforce 2026, the focus for AI agents has shifted from simple demonstrations to delivering measurable outcomes. Salesforce has integrated agents into a comprehensive platform that connects to enterprise data, workflows, and users, enabling outcome-based pricing, especially for service agents. Key insights from the event highlight how digital workers are becoming a significant part of the workforce, Slack is transforming into a central hub for enterprise agents, and Salesforce's Enterprise AI Harness provides granular governance for agent sprawl.

feed.title: Merck, Daiichi Sankyo withdraw US application for lung cancer therapy
feed.summary: Merck and Daiichi Sankyo have withdrawn their US application for accelerated approval of their experimental lung cancer therapy, ifinatamab deruxtecan. The decision followed discussions with the US Food and Drug Administration, which determined that mid-stage clinical study data did not meet the requirements for an early green light. The therapy was intended for adults with extensive-stage small cell lung cancer that had worsened after standard chemotherapy.

feed.title: Coca-Cola hires Rob Gehring from Monster Beverage to run its North American operations
feed.summary: Coca-Cola has hired Rob Gehring, formerly the head of Monster Beverage's Americas business, to lead its North American operations starting December 1. This strategic move comes as Coca-Cola aims to sustain growth amid rising gas and grocery prices impacting U.S. consumer spending. Gehring's experience at Monster, where sales climbed 20% in the second quarter, is expected to support Coke's efforts to innovate and expand beyond its core soda offerings.

feed.title: Tesla begins delivering Semi trucks to customers after years of delays
feed.summary: Tesla has officially begun delivering its Semi trucks to customers, with PepsiCo and DHL among the first to receive the electric heavy-duty vehicles. This milestone comes after years of delays since CEO Elon Musk first announced the project in 2017. The long-range Semi boasts a 500-mile range on a single charge, and Tesla plans to ramp up production to 50,000 units annually at its Nevada facility.

feed.title: Revenue rose 66%, but Indonesia Energy (INDO) says its liquidity is insufficient for at least a year.

Despite improved financial performance driven by increased oil production and higher crude prices, the company acknowledged that its liquidity remains insufficient for at least one year, raising substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a going concern. INDO plans to address this through operational efficiency, cost reductions, and potentially further ATM share sales, with $14.1 million currently available under its ATM program.
